design_rationale:
WORKLOG — air_ticketing_desk, task 1 (round 1).

STEP 0 — DRAW, ASSET LEDGER, SCOPE CLAIM.
draw_counts.py env/online_travel_agency/tasks/air_ticketing_desk --task 1 printed:
  {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}
So this task is a tree of two problems, one prerequisite, and each of its two computations rests on
exactly six declared factors. The design was written to that draw, never the other way round.

Occupied by task 0: air_ext_no_show_penalty, air_ext_unflown_tax_return,
air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit and air_ext_credit_release, with the tools
withhold_no_show_penalty_8882d2a1, return_unflown_taxes_e343d675, issue_travel_credit_599fe29f and
apply_travel_credit_e74c9b2a. That task claimed the whole cancellation, penalty, refund, voucher and
redemption ground, reading the club membership and the travel protection policy across difficulties.
Claimed here, from what was deliberately left free: air_ext_outstanding_service_charge and
air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay, with the tools settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa and
charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec. The two scopes are disjoint in policies, in tools, in base lineage
(air_service_fee, air_club_benefit_interaction, air_biz_exclusion, air_baggage_fee and
air_seat_and_cabin_extras here; air_penalty, air_refund_settlement, air_price_drop_guarantee,
air_credit_validity and air_agg_credit_pooling there) and in the cross-difficulty product they read
(the corporate programme here; the club membership and the protection policy there). With M = 2 the
difficulty closes on these two tasks and nothing is reserved for later.

Design thesis. Surface goal: the travel administrator of a small consultancy asks whether the four of
them can be moved into the business cabin on a ticketed Chicago to Paris itinerary. Scored core: the
co-payment collected for that move. Between the two lies one problem she never mentions — the booking
carries agency service lines for two of its four ticketed travellers, so the service charge is
incomplete, and the upgrade rule counts into the move only the travellers whose tickets the standing
lines already cover. Depth: goal -> co-payment -> the outstanding service charge, one hop stated by the
prerequisite sentence. Breadth: at both hops the number turns on the fare brand's own parameters, on
that booking's own ledger (which travellers carry a service line, which channel and currency the fares
were taken in, how many segments the fares run to, what bag was already bought) and on the firm's
corporate programme in another difficulty's product — its fee schedule, its rebate and overage
schedules, its seat allowance, its negotiated air discount, its approval levels, its credit limit and
its payment terms.

STEP 0 — BASE-INVARIANT CARD (rewritten in round 3; every base policy in every lineage is listed with
what it supersedes and what it still governs, so the card and `overwrite` say the same thing).

Subject air_fare_charge (the outstanding service charge). Governing base policies: air_service_fee,
air_club_benefit_interaction and air_biz_exclusion, none of which carries a structured eligibility gate,
so all three are inherited as policy_scope; air_ticketing is carried as input lineage, because its
collection clause is what makes the opening world legal rather than anything this policy supersedes.
  air_service_fee — superseded, declared in air_ext_outstanding_service_charge.overwrite: "The agency
  service fee is charged once per traveller on the booking at the moment the ticket is issued, and is
  stated separately from the airline fare and from taxes and carrier fees." (the charge here is owed for
  the travellers the standing lines do not cover, and is settled while the booking is still a hold);
  "The fee follows the fare brand held, not the cabin flown, so a business cabin sold under a saver brand
  carries the saver brand's fee." (the unit comes from the programme's own booking-fee schedule where a
  programme reference stands); and the conversion-markup sentence (the domestic markup applies where the
  contracting company is US-registered). Still in force: the fee is stated separately from the fare and
  the taxes, and it is not refunded when the traveller later cancels.
  air_club_benefit_interaction — nothing superseded by this policy and nothing owed to it here: this
  task's caller holds no club membership, no binding of either computation reads the club category, and
  the fall-through unit is the brand's own fee. It is cited because it governs the subject.
  air_biz_exclusion — superseded, declared in the same policy's overwrite: "a booking that carries a
  corporate programme reference is priced entirely on the programme's negotiated terms" (the conversion
  markup here is the policy's own domestic rate rather than the programme's). Still in force and
  honoured: the consumer/corporate price exclusivity that sends the unit to the programme's schedule, the
  rule that a brand not eligible for a corporate discount is still sold at its public price, and the one
  programme reference per booking.
  air_ticketing — nothing superseded; the opening world instantiates it. "Ticketing collects the fare,
  the taxes and carrier fees, and the agency service fee together; a partly collected booking is never
  ticketed": the booking has had its fares, its taxes and two of its four agency service charges taken,
  so it stands as an uncollected hold and base has not ticketed it. Its hold-window clause is honoured
  too — Premium Economy Select allows forty-eight hours, the booking was opened 2026-09-15 and frozen
  time is 2026-09-16 14:05, so the hold still stands and the "released without charge when it lapses"
  clause never engages on this world.
Subject air_ancillary_charge (the cabin move). Governing base policies: air_baggage_fee, which carries
the state gate booking_open_for_extras — "An optional extra is sold only while the booking record stands
at held or ticketed" — plus air_seat_and_cabin_extras and air_club_benefit_interaction, neither of which
carries a gate; air_biz_exclusion is carried as input lineage because this computation turns a corporate
programme into money. Authoritative evidence for the gate: air_bookings.status, correlated by
air_bookings.air_booking_id, which the tool takes as its air_booking_id argument. On this world the
booking stands held, which the gate allows; had it stood cancelled or travelled the correct terminal
state would be no upgrade line at all.
  air_baggage_fee — superseded, declared in air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay.overwrite: "A bag line already
  charged is refunded in full when the traveller cancels the whole itinerary inside the void window, and
  is otherwise refunded only where the flight itself did not operate." (a standing checked-bag line is
  credited against the co-payment). That quotation is not the gate's condition, so booking_open_for_extras
  is untouched and still carried in base_preconditions. Still in force: bags are charged bag by bag and
  traveller by traveller at the brand's rates, and bags presented at the airport are never charged here.
  air_seat_and_cabin_extras — superseded: "An upgrade into a higher cabin is sold only on a brand that
  allows it, at the brand's co-payment per traveller per segment, and never converts the booking to the
  higher cabin's brand terms." (the ordered shares act on that gross figure). Still in force and
  honoured: the move is sold only on a brand that allows it — Premium Economy Select carries
  upgrade_eligible true — and the booking is not converted to the higher cabin's brand terms, which is
  why the tool leaves cabin_class as it stands.
  air_club_benefit_interaction — nothing superseded and nothing owed: no club membership, no club read.
  air_biz_exclusion — superseded: "none of the consumer concessions in this charter apply to it" (the
  lead-time share is a consumer-side share applied to a corporate booking). Still in force: the booking
  is priced on the programme's negotiated terms, which is where the air discount, the approval share and
  the traveller share come from.
There is no time eligibility on either subject, so temporal_feasibility is [] and no anchor, counting
rule or boundary is in play. check_solvability confirms the required lineage and the gate set exactly;
the two extra lineage entries (air_ticketing on the service charge, air_biz_exclusion on the upgrade)
are declared for citation and override and add no precondition.

STEP 0 — BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
The narrowest object is the single air booking TM9XVB, the Chicago to Paris itinerary departing
2026-10-08, identified by its own air_booking_id, which both writes carry. Rows that enter the
aggregates: the two agency service lines (what the charge already covers, and the state the prerequisite
waits on), the eight base-fare lines (the channel, the currency and the two segments the move runs
over), the one checked-bag line (the credit against the co-payment). Rows excluded and why: the four tax
lines carry segment_sequence 0 and belong to no segment, so they cannot inflate the segment count; the
bag line is an optional extra and never a fare line, so it cannot reach the channel or currency reads.
On the programme's ledger the four invoices posted within twelve months are what the rebate reads, while
the 95,000.00 USD invoice of 2025-09-01 falls twelve whole months back and is excluded, and only the
September invoice carries a transaction count, so the overage reads the current month alone. Nothing on
this booking has been settled before: no upgrade line exists, and the service charge is incomplete,
which is what makes the prerequisite unmet.

STEP 0 — PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root: air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay (agent write, the move the caller asks for).
Edge: air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay <- air_ext_outstanding_service_charge, kind value_input, gate
covered_travellers, form state, resolved by settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa, owner user.
One prerequisite problem, matching the draw; one value_input edge against a floor of max(1-1,1) = 1.
Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the upgrade rule: "The co-payment for moving into a higher
cabin is worked out only after the booking's lines carry the agency service charge owed for every
traveller ticketed on it, and until that charge is complete only the travellers whose tickets the
standing lines already cover are counted into the move."
Four-point test: (1) it joins this policy's own result, the co-payment for moving into a higher cabin,
to what it waits on with the ordering connective "only after"; (2) the side it waits on is a
record-visible state — the agency service charge standing on the booking's lines — named in the words
the ledger and the finders use, with no action, performer or tool named; (3) it carries no tool name, no
policy id, no snake_case token and no row id; (4) its strength and scope are exactly the edge's: a hard
"only after", scoped to the service charge owed for every traveller ticketed, and it states in the same
breath what holds while the charge is short, which is precisely what the compute binding does.
State form, no fallback, so no fallback_reason. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state
about: air_ext_outstanding_service_charge is the only policy in the charter that puts an agency service
line on a booking, and its own rule says what that charge is and that it is owed once for every
traveller. Derivation: the sentence says the service charge must be complete; the records show two
service lines of 14.95 USD against four travellers ticketed, which is 29.90 USD where 59.80 USD is owed;
the service-charge policy's own rule says the charge is owed for the travellers the lines do not yet
cover; therefore the reader must first have that charge settled, and there is one reading only.
Seed evidence that the edge is false at the opening: initial_state.air_bookings.<TM9XVB>.passenger_count
= 4 against the two service lines of 14.95 USD each. The customer's own write: the settlement is
declared owner="user", because presenting a card is the traveller's own act; the desk unlocks it and
hands it over at the tree's first position, and it completes on the spot inside the same frozen clock.
Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the settlement leaves the co-payment at 686.25 USD
instead of 1406.25 USD, because only two of the four travellers are counted into the move.

STEP 1 — POLICY WRITING, AND THE FACTOR CARD.
Both policies declare their base lineage, the base clauses they supersede clause by clause in their own
`overwrite`, a baseline paragraph whose every sentence is verbatim in the rule, and six factors each.
The declarations are: air_ext_outstanding_service_charge supersedes air_service_fee's "The agency
service fee is charged once per traveller on the booking at the moment the ticket is issued..." with its
own owed-for-the-uncovered sentence, air_service_fee's "The fee follows the fare brand held, not the
cabin flown..." with its unit ladder, and air_service_fee's conversion-markup sentence with its own
markup ladder; air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay supersedes air_seat_and_cabin_extras' "An upgrade into a
higher cabin is sold only on a brand that allows it, at the brand's co-payment per traveller per
segment..." with its ordered-shares sentence, and air_baggage_fee's "A bag line already charged is
refunded in full when the traveller cancels the whole itinerary inside the void window, and is otherwise
refunded only where the flight itself did not operate." with its extras-credit sentence. None of the
quoted clauses is the condition of an eligibility gate, so booking_open_for_extras stays in force and is
still carried in base_preconditions. air_ticketing is carried in the service charge's lineage because
its collection clause is what the opening world instantiates rather than contradicts: the hold is partly
collected and therefore not ticketed, exactly as base requires.
FACTOR CARD (tier taken, evidence, and the figure the baseline would have given — all figures from the
Step 5 sensitivity run, recomputed by check_compute):
  air_ext_outstanding_service_charge (6 factors: 5 parameter, 1 method)
    programme_fee_schedule (parameter, biz)  tier 2: a programme reference stands and the base-fare lines
        were taken through the call centre -> the unit is the programme's offline booking fee, 29.00 USD.
        baseline: the brand's own agency service fee, 14.95 USD -> 41.86
    programme_billing_window (method, biz)  tier 2: the programme is invoiced monthly and its contract
        term, opened 2026-01-01, has run eight whole months, so its billing is read over the last twelve
        months, 168,400.00 USD. baseline: read over the current billing period alone, 52,000.00 USD,
        which carries no rebate at all -> 70.32
    programme_volume_rebate (parameter, biz)  tier 2: 168,400.00 USD billed over twelve months against a
        250,000.00 USD threshold, at least half of it -> half of 0.5 percent. The 95,000.00 USD invoice
        of 2025-09-01 is the near-miss the window excludes. baseline: no rebate -> 70.32
    programme_transaction_overage (parameter, biz)  tier 2: 180 transactions this month against an
        allowance of 250 -> half of 3.25 USD. baseline: nothing added -> 68.53
    short_notice_loading (parameter)  tier 2: opened twenty-three days ahead of departure and the brand
        carries an instalment plan -> the near-term loading of 10.00 USD. baseline: nothing -> 60.07
    settlement_currency_markup (parameter, biz)  tier 2: fare lines in euros and the company registered
        in the United States -> the domestic markup of 1 percent. baseline: no markup -> 69.48
    whole baseline -> 29.90, against gold 70.17
  air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay (6 factors: 5 parameter, 1 method)
    segments_moved_measure (method)  tier 1: a return date stands and the fare lines run to two segments
        -> the move is taken over both. baseline: one segment -> 686.25
    programme_air_discount_rate (parameter, biz)  tier 1: a programme reference stands and the brand is
        eligible for a corporate discount -> 4 percent. baseline: no discount -> 1466.25
    upgrade_lead_time_share (parameter)  tier 2: the outbound departs twenty-two days out, more than
        seven and not more than thirty -> the standard share. baseline: the late share of 1.15 -> 1622.25
    bought_extras_credit (parameter)  tier 1: one checked-bag line stands and the brand includes two bags
        -> the whole 45.00 USD credited. baseline: no credit -> 1440.00
    programme_approval_share (parameter, biz)  tier 1: two approval levels and a billing balance below
        the credit limit -> the whole figure. baseline: the unapproved share of 0.85 -> 1195.31
    programme_settlement_share (parameter, biz)  tier 1: a programme reference and payment terms of
        thirty days -> three quarters collected from the traveller. baseline: the whole -> 1875.00
    whole baseline -> 977.50, against gold 1406.25
Multi-source and cross-difficulty: every one of the twelve factors combines two conditions over distinct
evidence on every tier beyond the fall-through, and eight decide their tier from the corporate
programme's own record or ledger in another difficulty. The programme is seeded for this customer and is
read for values, not a bare existence: CPARAM on its booking-fee, rebate, overage, seat, discount,
approval, credit-limit and payment-terms parameters, CFIELD on its country, seat allowance and billing
balance, and XSUM over its billing ledger for both the twelve-month total and the current month's
transaction count.
No second product law was created: every tier condition reads a charter parameter (the brand's service
fee, conversion markup, instalment plan, upgrade co-payment, checked-bag allowance, seat-map release and
corporate-discount eligibility; the programme's online and offline booking fees, rebate threshold and
percentage, included transactions and overage fee, billing frequency and contract term, negotiated air discount,
approval levels, credit limit and payment terms) or the booking's own ledger.

STEP 2 — TOOLS.
Two tools, each with a freshly generated uuid8, each one atomic write.
  settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa (user): creates one agency service line and raises the booking's
    net paid total. Receipt: the line reference, the sum settled, the new net paid total.
  charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec (agent): creates one optional-extra line for the co-payment and raises
    the net paid total, leaving the cabin ticketed as it stands. Receipt: the line reference, the
    co-payment collected, the new net paid total.
Neither validates a prerequisite, checks a status or computes anything; see
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block. check_task_tools.py reports TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK over all six
tools of the difficulty.

STEP 3 — THE WORLD, AND WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW IS THERE.
customers: one profile, the caller, who is both the traveller and the programme's administrator.
air_bookings: the single held booking, carrying the corporate programme reference every biz read
hangs on; delete the reference and four factors fall to their fall-through tiers. air_booking_events,
fifteen rows: eight base-fare lines over two segments (delete the second-segment four and the method
factor falls to the fall-through and the co-payment halves), four tax lines carrying no segment (they
are what a careless reader might count into the segments), two agency service lines (the shortfall that
is the whole prerequisite; add two more and the edge lapses), one checked-bag line (delete it and the
extras credit falls to the fall-through). biz_programs: the programme whose schedule eight factors read.
biz_billing_entries, five rows: four inside the twelve-month window summing to 168,400.00 USD, of which
only the September one carries a transaction count, plus the 95,000.00 USD invoice of 2025-09-01 that
sits exactly twelve whole months back and is the near-miss — counting it would reach the rebate
threshold and move the customer to the top tier.
Automatic clauses checked before seeding: air_ticketing's advance purchase, stay limits and group
threshold all hold for this booking; its hold window is irrelevant because the booking is already
ticketed. air_agg_multi_holding ignites nothing, since the traveller holds one booking only.
air_baggage_fee's own clause that a bag already charged is refunded when the itinerary is cancelled
inside the void window ignites nothing, because nothing is cancelled. air_change_fee, air_penalty,
air_cancel_refund, air_credit_validity and air_price_drop_guarantee all rest on states this world never
reaches, so no obligation is lit that this task set cannot carry. No factor's tier is read off a stamp:
no row carries a field naming a fee schedule, a rebate tier or an approval outcome.
Cache design: amount_paid_usd of 5417.30 agrees exactly with the fifteen seeded lines and
credit_balance_usd is zero with no credit line; this task's history difficulty is reconciliation over
line kinds, channels, currencies and windows, not a stale cache.

STEP 4 — THE PERSONA.
Voice: brisk, numerate, faintly impatient, a caller with the file open who expects the desk to keep up —
deliberately a different register from task 0's tired, methodical traveller, and organised differently:
she states her request in her first breath and volunteers her constraints, where task 0's caller tells
her story first. Opening facts, all entailed by initial_state: four travellers fly Chicago to Paris on
the eighth of October and return on the eighteenth (departure_date, return_date, passenger_count); the
booking was made by telephone on Monday (booked_date, the call_centre channel on the fare lines); the
fares were loaded in euros (currency_charged on the fare lines); it is the firm's own corporate account
(corporate_program_id, biz_programs). Given only on request: the mobile number, the passport digits, the
date of birth, the postcode, the record locator, the corporate account number, the party composition,
the bag bought on Monday, and the firm's monthly settlement. She cannot answer how the programme's fees
are structured and says so, with the definite branch that the desk tells her the figure. Passive
reactions, each tied to an utterance the agent must make: she reacts to being told a service charge is
outstanding, runs the handed-over settlement herself and reads back the confirmation, then asks only
whether all four travellers are on the move once she hears it has been sold. Her last reaction answers
the last gold action and stops — nothing emailed, invoiced separately or added to a report. She never
states a figure gold uses, never names the prerequisite, and if a figure sounds wrong she says only that
it does not match her confirmation and asks for it to be checked. check_grounding reports GROUNDING OK.

STEP 5 — VERIFICATION, AND THE HANDLING-TIME RECOMPUTATION.
The harness replays the gold writes with the real tools onto the seeded database and evaluates each
policy on the snapshot taken immediately before its own step. Commands and output:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/online_travel_agency/tasks/air_ticketing_desk --task 1
    task comps fact xfac hist brch step match
    1.json   2   12    8   26   46   10  True      -> COMPUTE OK
  handling-time values: service charge 70.17 (step 7), co-payment 1406.25 (step 9);
  whole-baseline fall-backs 29.90 and 977.50; all twelve per-factor baseline substitutions move the
  result (figures in the factor card above); skipping the settlement takes the co-payment to 686.25.
The root problem's parameter was never evaluated on the opening world: on the opening world only two
travellers are covered and the co-payment is a different number, which is the whole point of the edge.
Arithmetic, longhand, at each handling time:
  service charge  29.00 x 2 = 58.00; 58.00 x (1 - 0.25/100) = 57.855; 57.855 + 1.625 + 5.00 + 10.00 =
                  69.48; 69.48 x 1.01 = 70.1748 -> 70.17
  co-payment      250.00 x 4 x 2 = 2000.00; 2000.00 x (1 - 4/100) = 1920.00; 1920.00 x 1.00 = 1920.00;
                  1920.00 - 45.00 = 1875.00; 1875.00 x 1.00 = 1875.00; 1875.00 x 0.75 = 1406.25
Two-way equivalence rule <-> compute. Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses,
crosses a category or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence it implements, and each
quotation was checked mechanically to be a whitespace-insensitive substring of its own rule. Reverse
sweep, sentence by sentence: for the service charge, the travellers not yet covered -> service_line_count
and travellers_uncovered; the unit and its three tiers -> unit_fee; the multiplication and the point at
which the rebate, the three additions and the markup act -> gross_charge, rebated_charge and result;
each of the four ladders -> its own binding; the floor and the rounding -> result. For the co-payment,
the co-payment per traveller per segment -> brand_copay, covered_travellers and segments_moved; the
ordered arithmetic -> gross_copay, discounted_copay, after_extras and result; each of the five remaining
ladders -> its own binding. No rule sentence carrying a quantity, window, filter, branch, order or
rounding semantic is left without a binding, and no binding carries a filter the rule does not state:
the twelve-month and last-month windows, the contract-term window, the base_fare, agency_service_fee and
checked_bag filters, the threshold at which the standing service lines are taken to carry the charge for
every traveller, and both roundings are all stated in prose. Where a semantic choice genuinely existed it is
pinned: the service charge states that the rebate acts on the gross charge alone, that the three
additions are added to the rebated figure and that the markup acts last on their sum; the co-payment
states the full order of the discount, the lead-time share, the extras credit, the approval share and
the traveller's share, and that the last of them acts last of all.

STEP 5 — SOLVABILITY CONTRACT AGAINST GOLD.
Two gold actions, one per problem. The settlement is state_due and cites the official record for intent
— four travellers ticketed against two service lines — while the cabin move is on_request and cites the
caller's own words verbatim. Its stage provenance is established_by_prior_tool, citing the settlement
step, because the travellers counted into the move are all four only once that charge is complete. No
stage fact is laundered: nothing waits on an approval, a clearing, a delivery or a future date, and both
writes land inside the one frozen clock. check_solvability reports SOLVABILITY OK with six base gates
checked and all sixteen primary rows audited.

STEP 5 — DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT.
With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and working only from the prose
the knowledge base will carry, the tool schemas, what the finders return and what the caller actually
says: she wants four travellers moved into the business cabin. The upgrade rule says the co-payment is
worked out only after the booking's lines carry the agency service charge owed for every traveller
ticketed, and that until then only the travellers the standing lines cover are counted. The ledger shows
two service lines of 14.95 USD against four travellers, so the charge is short and only two would be
counted; the service-charge rule says the charge is owed for the travellers the lines do not cover, and
it is the only rule that raises one. That gives the order settlement then co-payment, and the same two
figures fall out of the same ladders read against the same rows and the same programme record. The draft
agreed with gold at every step, and no ladder admitted a second reading: the tiers are pairwise disjoint
as stated and the customer sits on exactly one of each.

STEP 6 — EVALUATION AND CLOSURE.
Read nodes: the profile, the identity check, the booking, the whole ledger, the corporate programme and
its billing ledger — six reads, none duplicated, each feeding a named factor or the prerequisite. The
reads are also what reveal the prerequisite: the ledger read is what shows two service lines against four
ticketed travellers. Write nodes follow the topological order of the tree — the traveller's own
settlement first, the desk's upgrade second — each through its unlock/call pair.
Closure: policy -> target_tool -> computation.step/arg -> gold call -> terminal state holds for both;
set(computations.policy_id) equals charter_scope.extended_policies equals required_documents, in order;
charter_scope.task_tools equals the two tools in first-call order. No extra write and no idle policy
hangs outside the tree.

GATES RUN (per task, round 1, all from the repository root):
  check_extended.py  --task 1  -> EXTENDED OK
  check_task_tools.py          -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (6 tools)
  replay_tasks.py    --task 1  -> REPLAY OK (10 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors,
                                  closure 23 of 23 rows, match True)
  check_solvability.py --task 1 -> SOLVABILITY OK
  check_compute.py   --task 1  -> COMPUTE OK
  check_grounding.py --task 1  -> GROUNDING OK
  check_cross_fire.py --task 1 -> SCOPE OK

DIFFICULTY-LEVEL CLOSE (both tasks done).
Union of scopes: the six extended policies of the charter are covered exactly once each, and the six task
tools likewise; the two tasks share no policy, no tool and no customer. Every policy declared in
air.extended.yaml is claimed by exactly one task and recomputed at that task's own gold call. The suite
carries 4 and 2 computations, 19 and 12 declared factors, 35 and 26 reconciled history rows, 55 and 44
conditional forks and 16 and 10 actions, so the difficulty-wide means and maxima clear their floors with
room to spare.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT.
Taking the unit from the fare brand when a corporate reference stands on the booking. Reading the fare
channel off the bag line rather than the base-fare lines. Counting the 2025-09-01 invoice inside the
twelve-month window and jumping to the full rebate. Counting every invoice into the current month's
transaction figure. Reading the programme's billing over the current month alone when it is
invoiced monthly on a contract that has run eight months. Counting the four tax lines into the segments and making the move run over more than two.
Pricing the move for four travellers before the service charge is complete, or for two after it is.
Forgetting that the bag already bought is credited back, or that only three quarters of the figure is
collected from the traveller. Every one of these is settled by a sentence of the published rule read
against a row the finders return.


REVISION LOG — ROUND 2, answering the policy-task audit of 2026-09-16
(audits/policy_task/air_ticketing_desk/1.md and _difficulty.md).

user_scenario:
Delia Kastellanos runs the travel desk at Ridgeline Partners, a fourteen-person consultancy in Cambridge, and she travels on it herself. She is brisk, numerate and slightly impatient, the sort of caller who has the file open in front of her and expects the person on the other end to have it open too. Four of them fly Chicago to Paris on the eighth of October for a client engagement and come back on the eighteenth; she put the booking through by telephone with this desk on Monday evening because the fares were loaded in euros and the online tool would not take them.

She comes to the point at once. She wants to know whether she can move the four of us up into the business cabin for the Paris trip, and if she can, she wants it done on this call and charged now rather than sorted out later. She is happy for the desk to do whatever it is entitled to do on the firm's behalf, and she says so in as many words.

She gives her name, Delia Kastellanos, straight away, and when she is asked how to find the record she reads out the mobile number the booking notices go to, 7010883047. If a second detail is wanted she gives the last four of her passport, 1683. She can also give her date of birth, the second of November 1979, and the billing postcode, 02139, if either is asked for, but she offers neither unprompted. She knows the six-character reference off the confirmation, TM9XVB, and she knows the firm's corporate account number, RP4471QX, and reads out either on request.

She answers about the trip readily. Four travellers, all adults, two of them on a lower fare than the other two; nothing is ticketed yet and nothing has been flown; one checked bag was bought against her own seat on Monday and she remembers paying for that and for a cabin pet fee for a colleague's small dog separately. Asked about the programme she says it is Ridgeline's own corporate account and that the firm settles its invoices monthly. Asked anything about how the firm's fees are structured she says flatly that she has never read that schedule and that the desk should tell her, and she is content to be told the figure rather than to work it out.

She does not know how the move is priced, does not guess, and does not haggle. If the agent tells her there is an agency service charge still outstanding on the booking and that it has to be settled from her own card before the cabin move can be priced, she is briefly exasperated on principle, says that it should have gone on the original invoice, and then agrees to deal with it there and then. When the agent unlocks that step and hands it to her she runs it herself and reads back the confirmation that comes up on her screen.

Once she hears that the cabin move has been sold and charged to the booking she asks only whether all four travellers are on it, is satisfied by a plain yes, thanks the agent and ends the call. She asks for nothing to be emailed, invoiced separately or added to any report. If a figure sounds wrong against the confirmation in front of her she says only that it does not match what she is looking at and asks for it to be checked against the booking; she never says what it ought to be.

base_preconditions.condition: The service-fee policy governs every agency service line charged to a booking: the fee is charged once per traveller, it follows the fare brand held rather than the cabin flown, it is stated separately from the airline fare and taxes, and where the traveller is charged in another currency the conversion markup of the brand held is added and disclosed.

The club-interaction policy governs how a traveller club membership changes what a booking is charged, waiving the agency service fee or carrying a first bag free by the tier held on the ticket issue date; the traveller holds no club membership, so no tier is held and no club benefit reaches this line.

The corporate-exclusion policy governs a booking that carries a corporate programme reference: it is priced entirely on the programme's negotiated terms, none of the consumer concessions apply to it, and it may carry at most one programme reference. This booking carries exactly one, so the programme's own schedule is what prices this line.

The programme carries two approval levels and its billing balance of 18,240.00 USD stands below its credit limit of 75,000.00 USD, so the whole of the figure is carried forward. programme_volume_rebate (parameter, cross-difficulty): the billing so read, 168,400.00 USD, reaches half of the 250,000.00 USD threshold but not the whole of it, and the rebate percentage is above zero, so the second tier applies and half of 0.5 percent is taken off. The 95,000.00 USD invoice of 2025-09-01 is the near-miss the twelve-month window excludes: counting it reaches 263,400.00 USD, crosses into the first tier and produces 70.03 USD instead. The baseline takes no rebate and would have produced 70.32 USD.

programme_transaction_overage (parameter, cross-difficulty): the last month carries 180 booking transactions against an included allowance of 250, at least half of it but not the whole, and the overage fee is above zero, so the second tier applies and half of 3.25 USD is added. The baseline adds nothing and would have produced 68.53 USD.

short_notice_loading (parameter): the booking was opened twenty-three days ahead of the outbound departure, inside thirty but not inside seven, and Premium Economy Select carries an instalment plan, so the second tier applies and the near-term loading of 10.00 USD is added. The baseline adds nothing and would have produced 60.07 USD.

settlement_currency_markup (parameter, cross-difficulty): the base-fare lines were presented in euros and the contracting company is registered in the United States, so the second tier applies and the domestic conversion markup of 1 percent is applied. The baseline applies no markup and would have produced 69.48 USD.

Bindings belonging to no factor: travellers_carried reads the passenger count of four; service_line_count reads the two service lines standing; travellers_uncovered is their difference, two; gross_charge and rebated_charge carry the multiplication and the rebate; result floors at zero and rounds to the nearest cent.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and its fare lines were taken through any other channel
the programme is invoiced monthly or quarterly and its current contract term has run six months or more
the programme's billing so read reaches half of that threshold but not the whole of it and its rebate percentage is above zero
the programme's booking transactions counted over the last month reach half of that allowance but not the whole of it and its overage fee is above zero
the booking was opened within thirty days of the outbound departure but not within seven and the fare brand carries an instalment plan
the booking's fare lines were presented in a currency other than US dollars and the contracting company is registered in the United States

factor_trace: segments_moved_measure (method): a return date stands on the booking and its fare lines run to two segments, so the first tier applies and the move is taken over both. The cabin-pet line carries segment three but is not a fare line, so it cannot lift that count; a reader taking the maximum over every line would reach three segments and produce 2126.25 USD. The baseline takes the move over one segment and would have produced 686.25 USD.

programme_air_discount_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty): a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and Premium Economy Select is eligible for a corporate discount, so the first tier applies and the programme's negotiated air discount of 4 percent comes off the gross co-payment. The baseline takes no discount and would have produced 1466.25 USD.

upgrade_lead_time_share (parameter): the outbound departs twenty-two days from the handling date, more than seven but not more than thirty, and the brand releases its seat map before departure, so the second tier applies and the standard share leaves the figure as it stands. The baseline carries the late share of 1.15 and would have produced 1622.25 USD.

bought_extras_credit (parameter): one checked-bag line of 45.00 USD stands on the booking and Premium Economy Select includes two checked bags, so the first tier applies and the whole of that line is credited back. The 125.00 USD cabin-pet line bought the same day is the near-miss: it is an optional extra but not a checked-bag line, and a reader who credited every extra would reach 170.00 USD and produce 1312.50 USD instead. The baseline credits nothing and would have produced 1440.00 USD.

programme_approval_share (parameter, cross-difficulty): the programme carries two approval levels and its billing balance of 18,240.00 USD stands below its credit limit of 75,000.00 USD, so the first tier applies and the whole of the figure is carried forward. The baseline carries the unapproved share of 0.85 and would have produced 1195.31 USD.

programme_settlement_share (parameter, cross-difficulty): a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and the programme's payment terms run thirty days, so the first tier applies and only three quarters is collected from the traveller. The baseline collects the whole from the traveller and would have produced 1875.00 USD.

Bindings belonging to no factor: travellers_carried reads the passenger count of four; service_lines and service_line_count read what the booking's agency service lines now come to, and covered_travellers is the state the prerequisite sentence waits on — four once those lines reach the brand's own service fee taken once for each of the four, two before that; brand_copay reads the brand's co-payment of 250.00 USD; gross_copay, discounted_copay and after_extras carry the ordered arithmetic; result floors at zero and rounds to two decimal places.

a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and the fare brand is eligible for a corporate discount
the outbound departs more than seven days from today but not more than thirty and the fare brand releases its seat map before departure
checked-bag lines stand on the booking and the fare brand includes two checked bags or more
the programme carries two or more approval levels and its billing balance stands below its credit limit
a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and the programme's payment terms run thirty days or more

edges.condition: the agency service lines standing on the booking come to at least the fare brand's own agency service fee taken once for every traveller the booking carries, at the moment the co-payment is worked out
edges.policy_source: The co-payment for moving into a higher cabin is worked out only after the booking's lines carry the agency service charge owed for every traveller the booking carries, and until that charge is complete only the travellers whose places the standing lines already cover are counted into the move.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Only two agency service lines stand on a booking that carries four travellers: they come to 29.90 USD, short of the brand's own agency service fee of 14.95 USD taken once for each of the four, which is 59.80 USD. The charge is therefore not complete at the frozen handling date, and only the two travellers whose tickets the standing lines cover may be counted into the move.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the outstanding charge is settled, the booking's service lines come to 100.07 USD, at or above the 59.80 USD that the brand's own agency service fee taken once for each of the four travellers comes to, so the travellers counted into the move rise from two to four and the gross co-payment doubles from 1000.00 USD to 2000.00 USD.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge, so there is no pair of prerequisites to reorder and no freedom in the order at all: the co-payment cannot be worked out until the service charge standing on the booking is complete, and the prerequisite sentence of the upgrade rule states that outright. The verification run confirms it: with the settlement in place the co-payment is 1406.25 USD, and with it skipped the same formula on the same world gives 686.25 USD.
prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona raises one problem only, moving four travellers into the business cabin, and never mentions an agency service charge, a missing line or anything owed on the booking. It contains no question such as 'is anything outstanding' and no remark about the original invoice being incomplete. The traveller's whole contribution to the prerequisite is a passive reaction after the agent has explained it: she is briefly exasperated, says it should have gone on the original invoice, agrees to settle it, and runs the handed-over step. If the agent never discovers the shortfall she neither reminds nor presses, and the consequence falls on the terminal state alone.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the settlement and replaying everything else leaves the co-payment at 686.25 USD instead of 1406.25 USD, because only two of the four travellers are counted into the move, and the terminal state carries no service line either.

prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither task tool of this task validates a prerequisite. charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec is one ctx.create into air_booking_events followed by one ctx.update of the booking's running total; it reads no service line, branches on nothing and would post the upgrade against an incomplete service charge just as faithfully, for a different and wrong figure. settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa is the same shape and refuses nothing. The whole consequence of missing the prerequisite shows up in the terminal hash.
